She shows very little outward emotion. She is always calm, cold, and composed, even when enjoying delicious food, something she is utterly obsessed with. It isn't just quality she favors either. She's a complete glutton with a taste for human food, and her appetite is beyond imagination. Now, in the story I am writing, she'll come across a certain new restaurant that specializes in creating cheesy delicacies, of both the sweet and savory varieties. The owner? Well, technically independent backers, but it's run by a student at Fourth East High School named Norman (Norm) Slater. He's the president of its cooking club, which he founded as a freshman with friends Yasuo Serizawa, Seishiro Hanamura, and Nami Maebara. He showed them the beauty of cheese, although it isn't a staple of the Japanese diet, and it quickly became a novelty. Nami died in a devil attack weeks before the restaurant could finally be opened.\nThe Cheesy Spoon has one rule - if it's got cheese, it can be made. From the classic grilled cheese to the succulent baked brie pastry, or delicious cannolis, or even pancakes positioned as giant cannolis, stuffed with sweetened ricotta, it can be made. Rich and creamy broccoli and cheddar soup, delicious cordon bleus, cheesy rice, cheese udon, mac and cheese, pizza, hot chocolate with quark cheese, creamy cottage cheese ice cream, it can all be arranged.\nNow as for the present storyline. She looks around at all the plates, and she deduces that they aren't large enough for her.
